scenarios.title: Reverse when the first outlet is covered
scenarios.objective: Read the forecheck, then use the reverse only when far-side support is available
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. YOU have the puck below the left goal line. Gold 1 seals the near-wall lane; D2 is visible on the far side and W is higher.
cues: The puck is assigned to YOU below the left goal line.
Gold 1 blocks the near wall while D2 is visible across the crease-side lane.

questions.prompt: Which lane is Gold 1 visibly taking away?

options.text: The near-wall exit
The far blue line
The centre-ice faceoff dot

questions.explanation: Gold 1 is between YOU and the near-wall exit, so that lane is the pressure cue; the far-side option still needs its own check.

questions.prompt: Which two facts belong in the reverse decision?

options.text: D2 is available on the far side
Gold 1 is sealing the near wall
Whether W has already received the reverse

questions.explanation: D2’s location tells you whether a reverse has support, while Gold 1’s wall position explains the first restriction; the last shift does not change this freeze.

questions.prompt: Put one cautious reverse routine in order.

options.text: Check the far-side support
Protect the puck from Gold 1
Reverse only if the new lane is usable

questions.explanation: Protection buys a second look; checking D2 tells you whether the reverse helps; if D2 is covered, keep possession and choose another exit.

questions.prompt: Move D2 to an example support spot that keeps a reverse lane open.
questions.explanation: A lower far-side spot gives YOU a visible short option after the reverse; if Gold 1 tracks that lane, D2 must adjust again.

questions.prompt: If D2 is covered before the reverse, what should YOU reconsider?

options.text: Whether a protected hold or another support player is safer
Reversing anyway because the first lane was closed
Leaving the puck for the first teammate who calls

questions.explanation: D2’s coverage removes the intended receiver, so protection or a different support read preserves possession; if D2 reopens, the reverse can become available.

questions.prompt: What would you tell D2 before using the reverse?
questions.explanation: Call the pressure side and far-side support picture so D2 knows whether to present or stay low; if the call changes, the reverse decision changes too.

scenarios.title: Find the middle hinge after the rim
scenarios.objective: Use the middle hinge to connect a rim without skating into the carrier’s lane
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. D1 retrieved a rim at the left corner. YOU is low middle, D2 is higher, and Gold 1 steers the carrier toward the wall.
cues: D1 owns the puck in the left corner.
YOU are low middle; D2 is higher behind the play.

questions.prompt: Which player has the puck?

options.text: D1
YOU
Gold 1

questions.explanation: The puck is assigned to D1, so YOU’s job is support; if possession changes, the support read resets.

questions.prompt: Which two details make YOU a useful hinge?

options.text: A visible lane between D1 and D2
Distance that keeps you available below pressure
Standing directly on D1’s route

questions.explanation: A separated middle lane connects the defenders and leaves D1 room to carry; standing on D1’s route removes the support option.

questions.prompt: Order one hinge-support read.

options.text: See D1’s pressure
Show a middle passing lane
Adjust if Gold 1 closes it

questions.explanation: Pressure determines room; showing the lane gives a second outlet; a closed lane requires a new angle.

questions.prompt: Move YOU into an example hinge lane inside Gold 1 and clear of D1’s puck route.
questions.explanation: The inside spot gives D1 a short connection without copying the corner route; if Gold 1 cuts inside, widen or drop to keep a lane.

questions.prompt: If Gold 1 steps into the middle lane, what is a useful change?

options.text: Slide to a new support angle while D1 protects the puck
Stay hidden behind Gold 1 and call for a pass
Skate through D1’s stick lane

questions.explanation: Gold 1 removes the original hinge, so changing angle preserves an outlet; if the middle reopens, return without crowding D1.

questions.prompt: How does your support help D1 even when D1 does not pass?
questions.explanation: A visible hinge makes Gold 1 respect a second lane, giving D1 time to carry or connect to D2; if pressure ignores you, D1 can use the space.

scenarios.title: Stagger the regroup outlets
scenarios.objective: Stay at a different height from D2 so the regroup has two connected exits
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. D1 owns the puck just inside the left blue line. D2 is level with YOU near centre ice; Gold 1 shades the middle.
cues: D1 has possession near the left blue line.
YOU and D2 are at nearly the same height; Gold 1 shades middle.

questions.prompt: What makes the current regroup shape difficult?

options.text: YOU and D2 offer nearly the same height
D1 is behind the net
Gold 2 is below the goal line

questions.explanation: The level support lets one defender cover both lanes; if one player changes height, D1 sees a different outlet.

questions.prompt: Which two changes could create a connected second option?

options.text: Drop YOU below D2
Keep a lane between YOU and D1
Both forwards skate to the same dot

questions.explanation: A height change separates reads and a connecting lane keeps the regroup playable; one dot removes separation.

questions.prompt: Arrange one staggered support response.

options.text: Read Gold 1’s middle shade
Move to a different height from D2
Present the lane D1 can see

questions.explanation: Gold 1’s shade sets the need for space; changing height makes a second picture; presenting where D1 can see turns spacing into support.

questions.prompt: Move YOU below D2 to create a staggered regroup outlet.
questions.explanation: The lower position separates YOU and D2 and opens a different line to D1; if Gold 1 follows, preserve a connected lane.

questions.prompt: If Gold 1 follows your drop, what should you notice?

options.text: D2 may now be the open higher outlet
The same pass is automatically safe
Whether Gold 1 following makes D2 automatically open

questions.explanation: Gold 1’s movement can uncover D2’s height, so update the lane; if D2 is covered too, reset the regroup.

questions.prompt: Why is different height more useful than simply standing farther apart?
questions.explanation: Different height changes the defender’s choices and gives D1 a forward and backward connection; distance alone can leave one predictable pass.

scenarios.objective: Give a middle-driving carrier a second lane instead of skating into the same route
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. F1 carries over the right blue line with a middle drive. YOU is wide left, D2 trails high, and Gold 1 protects inside.
cues: F1 is the puck carrier entering from the right.
Gold 1 is inside F1; YOU are wide and D2 trails.

questions.prompt: Which lane is F1 trying to occupy?

options.text: The middle lane
The left corner behind the net
The wide lane beside YOU

questions.explanation: F1’s stated middle drive identifies the lane; support should protect a separate option beside it.

questions.prompt: Which two jobs fit YOU’s wide support?

options.text: Stay outside Gold 1’s inside position
Keep a passing angle back to F1
Cut directly through F1’s path

questions.explanation: Width gives F1 room and a visible release; crossing the route removes both options.

questions.prompt: Put one entry-support read in order.

options.text: Identify Gold 1’s inside position
Hold width beside F1’s drive
Adjust when lane or puck changes

questions.explanation: The defender’s inside position sets width; holding it gives F1 room; a changed lane requires a new route.

questions.prompt: Move YOU wider and slightly lower to support F1 without entering the middle.
questions.explanation: The wide-lower spot keeps F1’s middle route open and offers a wall-side option; if Gold 2 takes it, rotate behind the play.

questions.prompt: If Gold 2 steps into your wall-side lane, what is the next useful read?

options.text: Whether D2 can become safer high support
Whether to skate through F1
Whether the defender no longer matters

questions.explanation: Gold 2 removes the first support lane, so D2’s height matters; if D2 is covered, hold space and avoid crowding F1.

questions.prompt: How can wide support help a middle drive without receiving the puck?
questions.explanation: Width stretches Gold 1 and leaves F1 a release or carry lane; if the defence stays narrow, the wide lane may become the next pass.

scenarios.title: Delay the wall cycle until the low option appears
scenarios.objective: Use the low player’s position to decide when the cycle can connect below pressure
scenarios.briefing: Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. W has the puck on the right half wall. YOU is low near the end line, D2 is high at the point, and Gold 1 fronts the wall.
cues: W owns the puck on the right half wall.
YOU are below the puck near the end line; D2 is high.

questions.prompt: Where is YOU relative to W?

options.text: Below W near the end line
Above W at the point
Behind Gold 1 at centre ice

questions.explanation: YOU’s location creates the low cycle option; moving level with W changes that relationship.

questions.prompt: Which two relationships help a low cycle?

options.text: A low lane below wall pressure
D2 staying high enough to balance
W and YOU must both drop below the goal line

questions.explanation: The low lane moves the puck away from pressure while D2 balances above; crowding removes the next option.

questions.prompt: Order one low-cycle support check.

options.text: See whether W can protect the puck
Present below pressure
Reassess D2’s high balance

questions.explanation: W’s control decides whether a cycle exists; low support gives a release; checking D2 prevents an exposed point.

questions.prompt: Move YOU below and inside W to show a low cycle option.
questions.explanation: The lower-inside spot gives W a short route away from Gold 1 and keeps the net-side lane visible; if Gold 2 drops, move higher.

questions.prompt: If Gold 2 drops below W, what should YOU reconsider?

options.text: Whether the low lane is still open or higher support is safer
Cycling into Gold 2 because the puck is nearby
Leaving D2 with no balance

questions.explanation: Gold 2’s drop changes the low lane, so read coverage before moving; if it stays open, keep it available without forcing.

questions.prompt: What must W see before using your low option?
questions.explanation: W needs your separation from Gold 2 and a reachable lane without a blind pass; if pressure closes it, protect and wait for D2.

findings.issue: Every new-scene briefing uses '+x' and '-x' axis notation in player-facing text. U13 players should receive named-net language.
findings.evidence: All 25 exp26b-u13 briefings begin with 'Navy attacks the +x end and Gold attacks the -x end.'
findings.recommendedChange: Replace that sentence in each new briefing with 'Navy attacks Gold's net and defends Navy's net.' Preserve the actual net and actor geometry while removing coordinate notation from the player-facing scene.

findings.issue: The listed distractors are unrelated trivia, impossible guarantees, or automatic-certainty claims rather than credible U13 hockey decisions.
findings.evidence: Examples include 'The original faceoff result', 'Whether the bench door is open', 'The score from a previous game', 'A guaranteed open net', 'That the shot must go in', 'The goalie’s save is guaranteed', 'Changed teams', and 'The neutral-zone bench'.
findings.recommendedChange: Replace each affected distractor with a plausible nearby choice involving pressure route, support lane, puck protection, coverage handoff, or a conditional branch in that scene. Avoid guaranteed outcomes, irrelevant bench/game trivia, and choices that no player could reasonably select in the shown play.
